newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: POSSIBLE COMPENSATION FOR BLACKHAWK VICTIMS
The army's worst peacetime accident is prompting change.
The Government has announced an inquiry into military compensation and changes recommended may be retrospective so victims of the Blackhawk tragedy are covered.
The fiancee of the pilot killed in the Blackhawk Helicopter tragedy spoke out yesterday, but didn't want to talk about the compensation issue.
Leah Rose's was to have married Captain Kelvin Hales, one of 18 soldiers killed in the June counter terrorism exercise.
She says hopes the inquiry will ensure the tragedy which killed her partner never happens again.
MELBOURNE TO GET A$2 BILLION DOLLAR STADIUM
The Victorian Government is planning to outlay A$200 million on a sports stadium in hope of increasing its share of the 2000 Olympics spinoffs.
The stadium will be the centre piece of a major redvelopment of Melbourne's docklands.
The government will promote its central location, access to transport, and high tech facilities to attract some of the Sydney 2000 competition over the border.
VICTORIA STATE CARE SYSTEM NOT IN CRISIS SAYS REVIEW
The man who headed a review into the deaths of children under state care in Victoria says the system is not in crisis.
The Victorian Child Death Review Committee has spent the past six months examining the deaths of 15 children since 1994.
Its annual report also reveals that since 1989, 100 children in state care have died.
The report criticises a lack of training and communication breakdown within the Community Services Department.
MARTIN BRYANT IN COURT NEXT WEEK
The alleged Port Arthur gunman Martin Bryant is to be appear in the Supreme Court, in Hobart next Thursday, 12 days earlier than expected.
The Department of Public Prosecution says the new date has been set aside to discuss pre-trial issues.
His trial is scheduled for the 19th of next month and the DPP says its normal for such pre-trial discussions to be held running up to large criminal hearings.
Martin Bryant is now due to appear in court for a mention hearing on the seventh of November before the Chief Justice William Cox.
He's pleaded not guilty to all 72 charges relating to the April shootings, including 35 of murder.
CONCERNS OVER REEF RESEARCH PLAN
Conservationists say a plan to open up protected areas of the Great Barrier Reef to commercial fishing will devastate one of the world's natural wonders.
Scientists from Townsville's CRC Reef Research Centre want to study the effect of fishing pressure on eight marine reefs.
Under the plan, commercial and recreational fishing will be permitted in the pristine reef areas for the first time.
North Queensland Conservation Council Co-ordinator, Jeremy Tager says the experiment is another wild idea hatched by the CRC research centre.
He says CRC previously proposed an anchor damage experiment in which anchors would be dropped on pristine corals to see what the impact was.
SOUTH AUSTRALIAN MAYOR ALMOST APOLOGISES
A South Australian mayor whose comments on multi-culturalism sparked all bar one of his councillors to resign....has apologised....but not quite.
Port Lincoln Mayor Peter Davis has issued a letter of apology to those offended by his support for Independent MP Pauline Hanson...and comments such as mixed race marriages create mongrels.
But in the same letter of apology, to be published in today's edition of the Port Lincoln Times, he's re-stated his views, saying comments attributed to him have been distorted and inflamed.
He goes on to restate that Australia needs one people, one flag and one nation.
GOVERNMENTS SPARKING GAMBLING BUG, SAYS COUNSELLOR
It's claimed revenue chasing State Governments are contributing to Australia's gambling problem.
It's been shown Australians spend more money per person on gambling than residents of any other country in the world -- A$64-billion in total in 1994-95.
Addiction counsellor, Paul Symond, who's addressing a national conference on gambling in Sydney today, says Australians are a nation of gamblers because budget needs dictate it.
COMPENSATION CRACKDOWN ON NSW EMPLOYERS
WorkCover officers in New South Wales are preparing to crack down on employers who have ignored a three month amnesty and failed to take out workers' compensation insurance.
Today is the last day of the amnesty, and Industrial Relations Minister Jeff Shaw says WorkCover officers are to begin what described as a "blitz" on uninsured employers.
He says employers without insurance cost the state 20-million dollars a year, and warns those caught will also find the price high.
The maximum penalty for failing to obtain workers' compensation insurance is six months imprisonment and a 20-thousand dollar fine.
MELBOURNE HOSTING SEX EXPO
A four day expo on the sex industry opens in Melbourne today...and organisers say that never before has Australia hosted an exhibition of its kind.
They say all aspects of the adult entertainment industry will be covered at "Club X Sexpo", including health issues.
The Victorian Aids Council has thrown its support behind the event, and it's calling on exhibitors to promote material that doesn't encourage behaviour that could lead to the transmission of HIV.
TJANDAMURRA O'SHANE DOING WELL, SAYS SURGEON
Surgeons at Brisbane's Royal Children Hospital say the six-year-old boy who was set alight at a Cairns Primary school in far north Queensland, is doing well following substantial skin grafts.
They say they're awaiting the outcome of the grafts on Tjandamurra O'Shane.
Hosptial Director of Burns Professor Stuart Pegg says the grafts will be reviewed when Tjandamurra returns to the Operating Theatre for further grafts next Monday.
Professor Pegg says the skin used in the grafts was cultured in Melbourne from Tjandamurra's cells.
The operation was Tjandamurra's fourth major skin graft.
JAIL SUPERINTENDENT SACKED AFTER MASS BREAK OUT
The superintendent of a West Australian prison facility has been removed from duty by the State's Justice Ministry while authorities investigate a mass break out from the jail.
The Ministry of Justice has confirmed that Superintendant Ted Farr has been stood aside as head of Wooroloo Prison Farm after five prisoners escaped last weekend.
It's not known who's taken over as Superintendent.
Superintendant Farr's suspension comes amid widespread critcism of the W.A prison system by both police and the judiciary, after a weekend which saw twelve prisoners escape from four seperate jails.
